payload.problem_addressed: Exact-equivariant architectures encode prescribed group actions in specialized operators, complicating reuse with generic backbones and across data modalities.
payload.method_summary: GARI exposes selected transformation generators to a generic sequence backbone via aligned canonical and generator-induced views, formalized as a probe-specific soft-equivariance residual; GARI-Net builds generator-indexed streams, converts them to a common interaction frame, processes them with shared parameters, repairs ordering-induced context mismatch, exchanges information across streams, and aggregates via inter-stream discrepancy, with Direct Equivariance Error (DEE) as a frozen-checkpoint diagnostic.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces GARI, a representation-level interface that exposes transformation generators to a generic sequence backbone instead of hard-coding group actions into specialized operators. It formalizes a soft-equivariance residual and instantiates the interface as GARI-Net, using shared-parameter generator-indexed streams and a Direct Equivariance Error (DEE) diagnostic. Experiments across genomic sequences, images, and 3D point clouds (sequence reversal, planar rotations/reflections, axial transfer) show the same interface principle generalizes to held-out probes without group-specific backbone redesign.
key_architecture_choices: generator-indexed streams converted to a common interaction frame
payload.headline_results: Across these settings, the same interface principle supports task-relevant transformation consistency and generalization to declared held-out probes without requiring group-specific redesign of the sequence backbone.
claimed_advantages: portable across data modalities without group-specific backbone redesign
provides a diagnostic complement to hard-equivariant architectures
makes generator structure accessible, learnable, and measurable
limitations: finite-probe evidence remains distinct from certification of exact equivariance over a continuous group
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Our own native-rotation-invariance encoder line is closed, but GARI's generator-indexed-stream idea is a genuinely different mechanism: it could be layered on the existing B-rep graph-transformer encoder as extra generator-aligned views (e.g. for rotated/reflected face graphs) without redesigning the backbone, and DEE could serve as a cheap frozen-checkpoint diagnostic to quantify residual rotation/reflection sensitivity of the current encoder or of candidate deployment-time augmentation tricks.

payload.impact_rationale: A diagnostic/complementary equivariance mechanism, not a core fix for structural validity or program synthesis, so it would at best incrementally reduce residual rotation-sensitivity on an already-closed encoder line.
payload.effort_rationale: Porting generator-indexed streams + the DEE diagnostic from a generic sequence backbone to our graph-transformer B-rep encoder is a moderate prototyping effort (M), not a drop-in change.
